standard.title: Apply spoken conventions to enhance fluency
standard.description: apply knowledge of conventions of spoken target language to enhance fluency, and to respond to and create texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students apply sound and pronunciation knowledge for fluency — including complex vowel combinations, consonant conventions and regional variation (AC9LS6U01). They apply pronunciation in rehearsed contexts. They have not yet worked with sentence-level stress in extended utterances or applied written doubling conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply spoken target language conventions to enhance fluency — including consonant nuances, sentence-level stress, written doubling conventions and intonation for expression.

nodes.label: Consonant nuances, sentence stress and written conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish consonant pronunciation nuances, place stress correctly in extended sentences, and apply written doubling conventions in target language spelling.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two consonant pronunciation nuances; place stress correctly in at least two extended sentences; apply written doubling conventions correctly in at least two examples.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish consonant nuances in varied vowel and sound contexts; compare doubled consonant sounds with single equivalents; place sentence stress correctly in extended utterances; apply written doubling conventions in own writing and spelling.
wider: Read aloud a complex extended text with correct sentence-level stress throughout — demonstrating that stress placement is automatic rather than word-by-word
Compile a guide to written doubling conventions with examples — including the meaning and usage of key words
nodes.hinge_reason: Sentence-level stress and consonant nuance accuracy underpin intelligibility at the extended utterance level. Students with word-level accuracy but poor sentence stress sound unnatural and are harder to understand.

response_modes.reason: Sentence-level stress becomes automatic only through repeated extended production practice. Word-by-word accuracy does not automatically transfer to natural utterance-level stress.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two consonant pronunciation nuances correctly in spoken production
Places stress correctly in at least two extended sentences

nodes.label: Intonation and fluency in unfamiliar contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use rhythm, intonation and tone to enhance expression and fluency — including in some unfamiliar contexts — and apply these in their own spoken text creation.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a spoken text in an unfamiliar context with adequate fluency — demonstrating intonation and rhythm that conveys meaning beyond word-level accuracy.
nodes.typical_width: Use target language rhythms, intonation, tone and stress to increase fluency and expression; apply pronunciation to tongue twisters and performance activities; apply spoken conventions when creating texts; respond with adequate fluency in some unfamiliar contexts.
wider: Perform a tongue twister at full speed with correct stress, rhythm and pronunciation — demonstrating fluency beyond slow careful articulation
Create and record an original spoken text applying intonation, stress and rhythm deliberately for expressive effect

response_modes.reason: Fluency in unfamiliar contexts develops through varied speaking conditions. Fluency that only exists in rehearsed conditions is not genuine oral competence.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating original spoken texts with deliberate prosodic control is where spoken language becomes genuinely expressive — making the target language sound alive rather than performed.
success_criteria: Produces a spoken text with intonation and rhythm that conveys meaning and intention — not only lexical accuracy
Responds in spoken target language in an unfamiliar context with adequate fluency for communicative intent
